title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool + parallel calls with deterministic injection & retry semantics
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: Customers are increasingly composing multi-tool workflows (e.g. search + code-exec + db) with parallel tool invocation for latency. We observed two classes of problems in production: 1) non-deterministic tool-result injection ordering when parallel tool calls race, causing downstream model prompts to see partial/duplicated state; 2) brittle retry behavior that could double-execute non-idempotent tools or lose the correct tool result when retries returned different outputs. This PR makes the tool-calling execution model more ergonomic and robust: - Introduces a deterministic result-key ordering for injected tool outputs in the prompt scaffold when multiple tools are invoked in parallel. The order is stable (call order + tool priority tie-breaker) so downstream prompts and evals are reproducible. - Adds an execution envelope for each tool call: an idempotency token, wall-clock timeout, and best-effort canonicalization step for tool outputs to improve retry-safety. - Implements a retry policy change: retries are now only attempted for transient network/transport errors or explicit 5xx tool adapters; application-level mismatches (e.g. schema validation failures) do not trigger automatic retries. - Adds a merge-time buffer: the controller aggregates parallel results and performs a single injection pass into the model input, ensuring only one prompt update per call set. - Backwards compatibility: OpenAI-compat V1 calls retain previous behavior by default; we add an opt-in flag `stable_parallel_injection=true` to enable the new semantics for existing clients. - Tests & validation: new deterministic tests for multi-tool race scenarios, integration tests for idempotency tokens, and a canary rollout plan to enable the feature for 10% of traffic before full rollout. This is a behavioral, backward-compatible improvement to the hosted API and the compatibility layer; no customer-visible breaking changes expected unless `stable_parallel_injection` is enabled. Checklist: [x] design doc + benchmark, [x] unit & integration tests, [x] e2e canary plan, [x] docs update (compat and API notes), [x] perf regression <2% on p50 serving latency. See linked LINEAR items for more context.
